summary: Geant4 study statistics took standard errors from a seeded bootstrap of the events, estimated the most probable value with a five-point least-squares parabola whose bootstrap SE is not a consistent variance estimate, and had no exact intervals at low counts; the convergence gate, statistical target, detection limits and benchmark tolerances of a study rested on these numbers.

database_specific.introduced_basis: contracts 3.1.0 (Geant4 phase 2) made a study record re-issued validated-in-scope possible; it was first released in 0.20.0, and the affected scripts existed before without any record able to carry the label

observables: the standard errors, statistical target and detection limits of Geant4 study records
the most probable energy loss and deposit of thin-layer benchmarks
the value and statistical uncertainty of F4 design evaluations built on such studies
impact.bias: on J14 the bootstrap SEs were 15-20 % below the batch-means SEs of the same events (mean deposit 0.000193 vs 0.000237 MeV, tail fraction 0.00057 vs 0.00064); the thin-layer MPV detection limit was 0.0827 and is 0.0715 after the fix with the re-recorded runs
impact.trigger: any Geant4 study made with check_geant4_study.py summarize and geant4_benchmarks.py (bootstrap SE), most for most probable values and for tail fractions with few counts

applies_to.match_basis: a Geant4 study record carries extension.study and, from contracts 3.5.0, the check_geant4_study.py trace (a study record without validated-in-scope is listed too: its label was not upgraded, but its benchmarks and gate may still be affected); an F4 design-evaluation is built on such a record. A simulated dataset-record shows no field that tells whether its input study was affected: check its input study record instead

remedy: regenerate the study records with this version (check_geant4_study.py run and label --upgrade on run summaries from adapters/geant4/assets/summary_from_csv.py); after a study is re-issued, redo its F4 evaluations with evaluate_design.py f4 --replace (the old ones become stale once the study's hash changes); rerun contracts/dependencies.py on simulated dataset-records that use the study
